findings.problem: Adds 'what the Shepherd knows is good for him,' which the text doesn't say. Psalm 23:1 only says 'I shall not want.'
Reads like a pleasant devotional note. There is no Papa Dorin humor, hype or comparison, and 'a bold trust line' is generic.
Claims the Shepherd 'won't let him end up empty of what really matters.' This reads promises into the verse that the text doesn't state.
Says God's 'reputation' is 'on the line' and that His name means 'faithful, holy and good.' The verse only says 'for the sake of His name,' and the rest is added.
The 'flexing his muscles' line is a weak joke, and the rest is flat and explanatory. It could be funnier and more fatherly.
Says the rod and staff 'mean protection, guidance and rescue if he slips' and mentions 'the Shepherd's discipline and defense.' The text only says they comfort David. The meanings are added.
Preachy and generic with no humor, even though the Prep card sets up a joke about a big stick in a scary place.
Flat and mechanical. 'God is acting like a host laying out a meal, not pitching a tent' has no personality or laugh.
Says the host is 'taking His time' and gives 'careful, honoring attention.' The text doesn't say this, and it reads motives and manner into the verse.
Glosses mercy as 'His loyal love,' which is not in the BSB wording and adds a word the text doesn't use. It also says 'pursued by blessing.'
States the Bible fact that David lived in Hebron for part of his life with no reference. Every Bible fact needs its reference, such as 2 Samuel 2:11.
States 'The land is important in Israel's story' as a Bible fact with no reference.
Reads like a generic sermon line ('That's the destination his heart is set on'), with no Papa Dorin voice or humor.
